rival_explanations: A narrower equipment-only reading: the pole detects concrete physical equipment and building amenities named by count nouns (generators, radios, washrooms, busses) but not human support roles or administrative departments, so chaplains, counsellors and Human Resources should stay near zero while the amenity nouns still fire.

A broader institutional-provision reading: the pole detects any noun phrase naming something an institution supplies or maintains for its members, including abstract provisions such as scholarships, uniforms, timetables and regulations, so it should fire well beyond facilities and equipment.

package docker

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/grafeas/voucher/v2/docker/schema2"
	vtesting "github.com/grafeas/voucher/v2/testing"
)

func TestRequestManifest(t *testing.T) {
	ref := vtesting.NewTestReference(t)

	client, server := vtesting.PrepareDockerTest(t, ref)
	defer server.Close()

	manifest, err := RequestManifest(client, ref)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	schema2Manifest := schema2.ToManifest(manifest)

	assert.Equal(
		t,
		vtesting.NewTestManifest().Manifest,
		schema2Manifest,
	)
}

func TestRequestBadManifest(t *testing.T) {
	ref := vtesting.NewBadTestReference(t)

	client, server := vtesting.PrepareDockerTest(t, ref)
	defer server.Close()

	_, err := RequestManifest(client, ref)
	require.NotNilf(t, err, "should have failed to get manifest, but didn't")
	assert.Equal(t,
		NewManifestErrorWithRequest("404 Not Found", []byte("image doesn't exist\n")),
		err,
	)
}

func TestRateLimitedBadManifest(t *testing.T) {
	ref := vtesting.NewRateLimitedTestReference(t)

	client, server := vtesting.PrepareDockerTest(t, ref)
	defer server.Close()

	_, err := RequestManifest(client, ref)
	assert.NotNilf(t, err, "should have failed to get manifest, but didn't")
	assert.Equal(t,
		NewManifestErrorWithRequest("200 OK", []byte(vtesting.RateLimitOutput+"\n")),
		err,
	)
}

Intended for healthcare professionals

Clinical Review

Obesity in children. Part 1: Epidemiology, measurement, risk factors, and screening

BMJ 2008; 337 (Published 15 October 2008) Cite this as: BMJ 2008;337:a1824
1. Ruth R Kipping, research fellow1,
2. Russell Jago, senior lecturer2,
3. Debbie A Lawlor, professor of epidemiology13
1. 1Department of Social Medicine, University of Bristol, Bristol BS8 2PS
2. 2Department of Exercise, Nutrition and Health Sciences, University of Bristol, Bristol BS8 1TP
3. 3MRC Centre for Causal Analysis in Translational Epidemiology, University of Bristol, Bristol BS8 2BN
1. Correspondence to: R Kipping ruth.kipping{at}bristol.ac.uk

Summary points

• Population changes in physical activity and diet are probably the main drivers of the obesity epidemic

• A complex interplay of genetics; epigenetics; and intrauterine, infancy, childhood, and family non-genetic factors may also be involved

• Obesity in children and adolescents is associated with metabolic and cardiovascular abnormalities and other adverse health outcomes

• Modifiable risk factors for childhood obesity are maternal gestational diabetes; high levels of television viewing; low levels of physical activity; parents’ inactivity; and high consumption of dietary fat, carbohydrate, and sweetened drinks

• Obesity is commonly measured in children by plotting body mass index on a standard growth chart to adjust for sex and age using a defined cut-off point

• Population screening for childhood obesity is not recommended

Obesity was first included in the international classification of diseases in 1948. Since then, an epidemic has developed internationally, affecting all age groups. This article describes the prevalence of obesity in children, its underlying risk factors, its consequences, and how it can be measured; it also discusses whether children should be screened for obesity. In a second article to be published next week we will discuss the prevention and management of obesity in children.1 The terms used are defined in box 1 (where authors of cited papers use terms differently we use the authors’ own words).

Sources and selection criteria

This review draws on the Foresight report, guidance from the National Institute of Health and Clinical Excellence, and a Cochrane review of preventing obesity.

In April 2008 we searched the Cochrane Library database of reviews and the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination databases using the search term “obesity”. We also conducted a Medline search ((Child$or paediatric or pediatric or adolescent) and (Obes$ or overweight)) limited to 1 January 2005 to 6 May 2008 and “review articles”; this identified 1105 articles. We read the abstracts of these articles and retrieved relevant papers. We also used articles from our own bibliographies collected over the past 10 years.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The university's student-services office provides chaplains, counsellors and financial-aid advisors to any undergraduate who asks for help, and the appointments are free of charge all year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Prototypical positive: support roles (chaplains, counsellors, financial-aid advisors) that an institution provides to its members, at the completion of each compound.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Every new hire meets the Human Resources team on the first morning, and the department explains the pension scheme and the holiday schedule in some detail.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive for a named service department provided by the employer to its staff, peaking on 'Resources' at the completion of 'Human Resources'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hospital inspects its washrooms twice a day, and the cleaners replace the soap and the paper towels whenever they finish a round of the wards.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive for a facility the institution inspects and maintains, matching the claimed boost from a passage about upkeep.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The base maintains its signalling equipment, generators and radios in a shed behind the barracks, and a technician checks every unit before the winter sets in.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive for concrete equipment (equipment, generators, radios) that an institution maintains for its members.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The monastery provides three meals a day to its novices, and the kitchen staff post the menu on the refectory door every Sunday morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive for meals supplied to members by an institution, a provision that is neither a human role nor equipment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The company runs busses from the car park to the office every twenty minutes, and employees ride them for nothing at all.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive for a transport amenity the institution runs for its members, peaking on the plural amenity noun.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language positive: Spanish sentence naming chaplains, counsellors and scholarship advisors provided by a university to its students.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Het ziekenhuis stelt aan zijn patiënten kapelaans, vertrouwenspersonen en maatschappelijk werkers ter beschikking, elke dag van de week en zonder afspraak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The refuge keeps a full-time advocate on site for residents who need help with their asylum paperwork, and a night warden who checks the dormitories.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout: support roles (advocate, night warden) expressed with words absent from the claimed token list, provided by an institution to its residents.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Prospectus, 2019 edition. The school was founded in 1887 by a group of local merchants and moved to its present site forty years later, when the main hall and the science block were built. Over the following decades the buildings were extended several times, and the governors record with gratitude the generosity of former pupils who paid for the library and the swimming pool. Pastoral care has always been central to the school's reputation, and the staff take pride in knowing every pupil by name, whatever house they belong to and whichever subjects they choose in the sixth form. In the senior school a team of chaplains, counsellors and learning-support advisors is available throughout the week, and any pupil may arrange a conversation without telling a teacher first. Boarders have additional access in the evenings, when a duty tutor is always on call and a resident housemaster sleeps in each boarding house. Parents are welcome to write directly to the head of pastoral care if they have a concern, and the school aims to reply within two working days. The admissions office will send a full list of staff on request, together with the dates of the open mornings and the procedure for applying for a place. Visitors are asked to sign in at the lodge and to park beyond the chapel, where there is room for about thirty cars. The governors review these arrangements each year and publish a short summary in the spring newsletter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context positive in a different genre (a school prospectus): the support roles appear deep inside a passage that describes the institution's pastoral provision.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: 'resources' in the natural-resources sense, with no service department and no institution providing anything to members.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The defendant's counsellors asked for more time to prepare their case, and the judge agreed to postpone the hearing until Monday morning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hikers cooked their meals on a small stove beside the tent and were asleep in their bags before the last light had gone.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The society's annual meeting approved the budget, thanked the treasurer for her work and agreed to hold next year's gathering in the same week as the summer fair.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The thieves cut the padlock, loaded the generators onto a truck and drove off before the guards had finished their round of the yard.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: 'generators' as stolen equipment, with no institution providing, inspecting or maintaining them.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The prisoners were denied visits, letters and radios, and the warders searched the cells for anything that could be used to signal outside.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Notes for parents, revised edition. The governors have asked us to set out again how the school handles the practical side of membership. Each year the foundation offers four scholarships to children from the town, and the awards cover fees, books and the cost of the annual excursion to the coast. Every pupil is issued with a uniform at the start of the first term, and replacements can be ordered by post at any time, though the colours change only once a decade. The timetable is published in the last week of August, and a printed copy is given to each family on the first morning. A separate sheet explains the regulations that govern absence, lateness and the borrowing of books; these are reviewed by the governors every third year, and any change is announced in the newsletter. Families are asked to read the sheet carefully, to sign the last page and to return it before the end of the first week of term. Signed forms are counted by the clerks, and the totals are reported at the autumn meeting of the governing body. The school thanks parents for their patience while these arrangements were revised, and asks them to keep the summary with the other papers they receive during the year. A further revision is expected in three years, when the current regulations expire and the foundation must decide how much money it can set aside for awards.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long hard negative: a passage full of provisions an institution supplies (scholarships, uniforms, timetable, regulations) but none is a support role, service department, facility or equipment, so the hypothesis predicts silence while the broad rival predicts firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At about three o'clock the clouds that had been building all morning finally broke, and the rain came down hard on the fields. The harvest had been late that year, and most of the corn still stood in the rows waiting for the machines. The farmer and his two sons watched from the yard, then went back into the barn to repair a harness that had torn during the week. In the afternoon the wind dropped as suddenly as it had risen, the sun appeared again, and the water lay in bright sheets across the lower field, where the stream had overflowed its bank during the night. By evening the ground had begun to dry, and the family walked out to see how much had been flattened and whether the fence at the bottom of the meadow was still standing. They decided to leave the rest until Monday and to hope for a clear weekend, since the forecast promised nothing but more rain, and the neighbouring farms had already lost a good part of their crop. The eldest son drove into the village to ask whether anyone had a spare part for the baler, but the workshop was shut and the owner had gone to a wedding in the next county. He came back with nothing and went to bed early, and by midnight the sky had cleared and the stars came out over the quiet fields.

readings.explanation: Retrospective detector for noun phrases naming support roles, service departments, facilities, or equipment that an institution provides to its members (e.g. chaplains, counsellors, financial-aid advisors, Human Resources, washrooms, meals, busses, generators, radios), typically peaking at the completion of the compound; strength is boosted when the surrounding passage describes the institution providing, inspecting, or maintaining them, consistent with its staff/logistics output direction and heavy long-range attribution.

A narrower equipment-only reading: the pole detects concrete physical equipment and building amenities named by count nouns (generators, radios, washrooms, busses) but not human support roles or administrative departments, so chaplains, counsellors and Human Resources should stay near zero while the amenity nouns still fire.

A broader institutional-provision reading: the pole detects any noun phrase naming something an institution supplies or maintains for its members, including abstract provisions such as scholarships, uniforms, timetables and regulations, so it should fire well beyond facilities and equipment.
